speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) how many Employment Pass and S Pass holders have submitted fabricated or forged education qualification certifications in the past three years in the ICT industry; and (b) whether the Ministry will review and work with only reputable overseas educational institutions with a proven track record for approval of both Employment Pass and S Pass applications.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: All employers have the primary responsibility to ensure the authenticity and quality of their candidates’ qualifications when submitting work pass applications.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: MOM also conducts additional checks by screening the qualifications submitted through our database of institutions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This database is reviewed regularly through our scan of open source reports and research from third-party screening organisations.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: MOM takes a firm stance against foreigners who submit false qualifications to fraudulently obtain work passes.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Can MOM also elaborate whether they would review their process to pick up the cases faster?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: These verification agencies have been pre-assessed by MOM and they are listed on our MOM website.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: If there is no verification proof that confirms that the diploma and degree qualifications declared are genuine, the application will be rejected.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Of course, there are those on a lower-risk and those that are medium-risk.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: At different categories, we have a different response mechanism.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: When MOM classifies educational institutions by risks, what is the basis for that classification?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Is it that certain educational institutions are deemed to be sort of less reputable or less well-accredited and, therefore, they are deemed to be higher-risk and, therefore, third-party verification will be required by the employer?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: If so, then what is the assurance that lower-risk institutions may not also be subject to fake educational credentials?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: For example, someone may fake a degree from a well-known or reputable university.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: So, what is the assurance in those cases?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: My supplementary question is, really, what is the basis for this risk tiering?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For accreditation checks, we have maintained a database over the years as we screened the qualifications, whenever employers submit the respective to-be-hired employees' qualifications.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Over the years, as we built the database, we have within our system and also, we compare them with the database from third-party verification agencies that we work closely with.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I have also said earlier on that the list of these third-party verification agencies is available on our website.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, through the years, we have built that.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We use a combination of data analytics; we screen them.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And from that, we then ascertain a risk stratification strategy in which we match all of these applications when they come to us through this database that we have.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Obviously, we do not do this on 100% of all applications submitted, but based on our predictive analytics, when we find that there is reason for us to have suspicion – and we do have a very high index of suspicion – we then activate this other route where we actually call them for independent checks.
